code_label: Real-data benchmark across multiple solvers
text_span: we implement a number of quantum and quantum-inspired algorithms on different hardware platforms to solve its discrete formulation using real data from daily prices over 8 years of 52 assets
rationale: States the central empirical setup and benchmarking design.

code_label: Comparison across performance metrics
text_span: do a detailed comparison of the obtained Sharpe ratios, profits and computing times
rationale: Identifies the main evaluation criteria used in the study.

code_label: First tensor-network application in this context
text_span: for the first time in this context also a quantum-inspired optimizer based on Tensor Networks
rationale: Highlights a novel methodological addition claimed by the authors.

code_label: Clustering-based dimensionality reduction
text_span: we also consider doing a preprocessing based on clustering of assets
rationale: Captures the preprocessing decision used to fit data to hardware constraints.

code_label: Largest systems handled by two methods
text_span: D-Wave Hybrid and Tensor Networks are able to handle the largest systems
rationale: Summarizes a headline comparative finding about scalability.

code_label: Dynamic objective includes transaction costs and constraints
text_span: taking into account transaction costs and other possible constraints
rationale: Defines the problem setting as dynamic and constrained.

code_label: Problem is intractable in generic cases
text_span: In practice, it is well-known that this is an intractable problem for generic instances
rationale: States a motivating difficulty of the optimization problem.

code_label: Quantum and quantum-inspired computing may help finance
text_span: it has been understood recently that quantum and quantum-inspired computing can help in solving hard financial problems
rationale: Provides the broader motivation for applying these methods.

code_label: No prior open comparison on real datasets
text_span: no comparison has ever been done openly and democratically between different methods and hardware platforms
rationale: Claims a gap in prior work that this paper addresses.

code_label: Hamiltonian decomposes by time step
text_span: the Hamiltonian is diagonal in time
rationale: Important structural observation enabling per-time-step optimization.

code_label: Continuous formulation is exactly solvable without transaction costs
text_span: if this is the case, then the problem can be solved analytically (in the continuous variable limit)
rationale: States an analytical solvability result for a simplified case.

code_label: Discrete formulation maps naturally to QUBO
text_span: the problem is therefore equivalent to finding the ground state (i.e. the minimum over the variables {xn,t,q}) of the classical Hamiltonian
rationale: Describes the discrete encoding used for quantum and quantum-inspired solvers.

code_label: Discrete problem is NP-hard in the generic case
text_span: Ising spin-glasses are known to be NP-Hard in the generic case
rationale: States the computational complexity of the mapped problem.

code_label: Classical solvers used as benchmarks
text_span: The classical methods were implemented as a benchmark of the rest of the algorithms
rationale: Explains the role of classical baselines in the study.

code_label: D-Wave Hybrid overcomes processor size limits
text_span: The D-Wave Hybrid algorithm uses a hybrid classical-quantum strategy to overcomes this limitation
rationale: Describes the hybrid annealing strategy used to scale beyond hardware limits.

code_label: VQE implemented on IBM-Q with custom ansatz
text_span: we implemented VQE optimization in the quantum processors of IBM-Q, up to 12 qubits
rationale: Specifies the gate-based quantum implementation and its scale.

code_label: VQE circuit uses strongly entangling layers
text_span: It is based on a strategy of strongly entangling layers
rationale: Identifies the circuit design choice for the variational ansatz.

code_label: VQE-Constrained samples low-energy states then recombines them
text_span: use VQE to sample several low-energy states at every rebalancing time t, and then use a classical approach to find which combination of these provides the highest returns
rationale: Captures the hybrid post-processing strategy introduced by the authors.

code_label: Tensor networks represent states with fewer parameters
text_span: Constructed in this way, the TN depends on O(poly(n)) parameters only
rationale: Explains the compression principle behind the tensor-network approach.

code_label: Tensor networks used as optimization ansatz
text_span: we implemented an optimization strategy over the so-called Matrix Product States
rationale: States the specific tensor-network family used for optimization.

code_label: Real dataset spans 52 assets over 8 years
text_span: Our dataset consists of the daily values of 52 assets over 8 years
rationale: Describes the empirical dataset used in the experiments.

code_label: Log returns preferred over bare returns
text_span: logarithmic returns are preferred over the bare returns
rationale: Records a data-preparation choice for return calculation.

code_label: Low-variance low-return assets removed
text_span: By discarding assets which simultaneously have sub-average variance and sub-average returns, our dataset can be reduced from 52 down to 28 relevant assets
rationale: Shows a filtering step used to reduce problem size.

code_label: Clustering chosen around six to eight groups
text_span: We therefore take ≈6 −8 as a reasonable choice of number of clusters for this dataset
rationale: States the selected clustering granularity.

code_label: Clustering applied only to limited-hardware methods
text_span: we only applied this clustering for specific methods and hardware, namely, for the ones that could not handle the full problem being analyzed
rationale: Explicitly limits where preprocessing was used.

code_label: Monthly rebalancing and 20-day covariance window
text_span: We will consider the portfolio rebalancing to happen once monthly
rationale: Specifies the temporal resolution and estimation window choices.

code_label: Results compared by dataset size
text_span: we built datasets of different sizes. We considered datasets of size XS, S, M, L, XL and XXL
rationale: Describes the scaling experiment design.

code_label: Risk aversion fixed for all simulations
text_span: for the sake of simplicity, we set the risk aversion parameter γ = 1
rationale: Notes a fixed hyperparameter across experiments.

code_label: Energy minimum does not always match profit or Sharpe
text_span: the solution which minimizes the cost function H does not always extremize the profit, returns, and Sharpe ratio
rationale: Important analytical observation about differing objective metrics.

code_label: Gekko can outperform quantum methods on some metrics
text_span: the performance of Gekko is quite remarkable, sometimes even better than quantum and quantum-inspired solutions depending on the metric
rationale: Reports a comparative finding favoring a classical solver in some cases.

code_label: Gekko hits a memory wall
text_span: the method hits a memory wall around 500 qubits
rationale: States a scalability limitation of the classical solver.

code_label: D-Wave Hybrid and tensor networks scale to 1272 qubits
text_span: with today’s D-Wave Hybrid as well as with our TN algorithm we optimized up to 1272 fully-connected qubits
rationale: Key scalability result for the two largest-capacity methods.

code_label: VQE struggles on commercially relevant dimensions
text_span: a naive application of universal quantum processors such as IBM-Q still struggle to tackle optimization problems of commercially relevant dimensions
rationale: States a limitation of the gate-based quantum approach.

code_label: D-Wave Hybrid is fast on the largest dataset
text_span: D-Wave Hybrid allows us to solve problems up to 1272 fully-connected qubits in 171 seconds
rationale: Reports a concrete runtime result for the hybrid solver.

code_label: Tensor networks can be accelerated substantially
text_span: we can reduce at least ≈100× the run-time of our TN algorithm
rationale: States a projected performance improvement.

code_label: No clear best algorithm across metrics
text_span: there seems to be no clear answer as to which is the “best” algorithm and hardware platform to solve the dynamic portfolio optimization problem for large systems
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s comparative conclusion.

code_label: Hybrid approaches are especially promising
text_span: hybrid quantum-classical solutions (both in hardware and software) are offering the best operational performances
rationale: Highlights the authors’ assessment of hybrid methods.

code_label: Future hybrid quantum-TN combination
text_span: a hybrid approach combining quantum processing and Tensor Networks should be quite successful for many problems
rationale: Identifies a proposed next-step direction.
